algorithm.Title: Foot Pain - Female (Child)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Child | Female
Definition: UAT-only adult and pediatric non-traumatic foot-pain pathway screening for infection, inability to bear weight, neurovascular compromise and diabetic or immune risk before in-person assessment.
FirstAid: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 for systemic illness with hot swelling, inability to bear weight, severe rapidly worsening pain, or a cold/pale/blue/numb foot. Do not allow self-driving. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.

questions.Question: Did this joint problem begin with a motor vehicle crash or as part of a multi-system crash injury?
questions.Information: A motor vehicle crash or multi-system crash injury belongs in the Motor Vehicle Accident pathway.

questions.Question: Is foot pain severe with inability to bear weight or a cold/pale/blue/numb foot, or is there a diabetic/other wound or hot swelling plus marked systemic illness or rapid deterioration?
questions.Information: NHS.UK joint pain guidance lists swelling/heat and feeling unwell as reasons for urgent review; diabetic foot problems specifically need prompt assessment given the higher risk of complications.

questions.Question: With no emergency feature, is there any persistent or unexplained foot pain, wound, swelling, walking limitation, diabetes/immune risk, child concern or higher-risk context?
questions.Information: In-person assessment is required, particularly for diabetes/neuropathy, wounds, immune risk, children and impaired weight bearing.

advice.Title: Qatar emergency foot response
Content: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 for systemic illness with hot swelling, inability to bear weight, severe rapidly worsening pain, or a cold/pale/blue/numb foot. Do not allow self-driving. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
Call Back If: increasing swelling or redness; fever or neurovascular change.

advice.Title: In-person foot assessment
Content: Arrange in-person assessment, especially for a child, pregnancy, diabetes, neuropathy, immune compromise or skin break. Protect from pressure and do not use fixed-dose analgesia until patient factors are checked.
Call Back If: pain persists or worsens; swelling, redness or fever.

references: NHS.UK, "Joint pain", https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/joint-pain/ (page last reviewed 26 February 2026) - applied to non-traumatic foot pain
